partner_context.their_ambition: You run one of the world's most ambitious mobility programmes — metro, tram, abras, ferries and water buses — toward the Dubai 2040 '20-minute city.' Your Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 explicitly targets a 51% rise in marine ridership (14.7M → 22.2M/yr) and a 400% increase in passenger lines.
partner_context.their_pressure: Both growth and UAE Net Zero 2050 demand fleet renewal and new high-value corridors from you — without disturbing the heritage abra trade that makes Dubai's water unique.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the premium, zero-emission, software-defined edge of that renewal: fast corridors today's fleet can't serve, fully additive to your abra cooperative and aligned to your Marine Plan 2030 targets.

hero.title: Dubai RTA × Navier — a premium, zero-emission layer on the water
hero.subtitle: A foiling tier that sits above today's marine network — new high-value corridors, a clear decarbonization path, and the abra trade left untouched.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a software-defined hydrofoiling tier to Dubai's marine transport network: quiet, zero-emission, and fast. It opens premium corridors the current fleet can't serve — a fast Creek premium service and a Dubai-to-Abu Dhabi express — and gives the authority a credible decarbonization path for water-bus and ferry renewal, all additive to existing services and fully aligned with Dubai 2040 and UAE Net Zero 2050.

why_now: Dubai 2040 sets a '20-minute city' goal and an expanding marine network; UAE Net Zero 2050 mandates decarbonization across every mode. Foiling is the premium edge of that renewal — faster and more efficient per passenger-mile, near-silent, zero-emission, and proven at network scale in the Maldives (2026). A demo vessel is in Dubai now.

objections.concern: Will this disrupt the abra trade?
objections.response: No — the foiling tier sits above the heritage trade on premium corridors the abras don't serve. It is purely additive and protects the cooperative.
Pioneer II needs only a home-berth pedestal; Quanta-LR's hybrid range covers the long Dubai↔Abu Dhabi leg with no offshore charging at all.
Every inner-Dubai corridor is a few nautical miles; Dubai↔Abu Dhabi (~60 nm) is within Pioneer II range, Quanta-LR beyond. Climate-controlled cabins and far lower energy per mile handle the summer.

objections.concern: Is a foiling vessel safe in Dubai's busy, shared waterways?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil zones near abra lanes and berths, automatic speed/wake limits in shared water, and full-hull-down low-speed manoeuvring. The vessel flies only on the open corridors where it's cleared to, and drops to a conventional displacement craft everywhere else.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring network integration, berth access, the Marine Plan 2030 mandate and regulatory cover.
the_ask.next_step: A Creek premium pilot, co-specified with RTA against the Marine Plan 2030 targets.

close.title: A premium water layer that grows with the city.
close.body: Start on the Creek, scale across the inner network, then connect the capital — a zero-emission foiling tier that advances Dubai 2040 and Net Zero 2050 while protecting the heritage trade that makes Dubai's water unique.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
